« Je suis en paix avec ma décision » : Romelu Lukaku quitte la sélection belge !

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (543 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Le10sport

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • C'est une annonce majeure pour le football belge en ce lundi 16 novembre 2026.
  • L'attaquant de 33 ans a surpris l'ensemble des observateurs au lendemain de la victoire de la Belgique face à l'Italie (4-1) en Ligue des nations, qui a validé la qualification des Diables Rouges pour les quarts de finale du tournoi.
  • En quittant la sélection, Romelu Lukaku laisse un héritage statistique considérable.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

C'est une annonce majeure pour le football belge en ce lundi 16 novembre 2026. Sur son compte Instagram, Romelu Lukaku a officialisé son départ définitif de la sélection des Diables Rouges après seize années passées au plus haut niveau international.

L'attaquant de 33 ans a surpris l'ensemble des observateurs au lendemain de la victoire de la Belgique face à l'Italie (4-1) en Ligue des nations, qui a validé la qualification des Diables Rouges pour les quarts de finale du tournoi. Dimanche 15 novembre 2026, Romelu Lukaku est resté sur le banc des remplaçants sans entrer en jeu, après avoir manqué le match précédent face à la Turquie en raison d'une légère blessure à la hanche. Pour accompagner son message d'adieu sur le réseau social, le joueur a publié une galerie photo retraçant son parcours international depuis ses débuts en mars 2010 à l'âge de 16 ans. Plusieurs coéquipiers emblématiques de la génération dorée, dont Axel Witsel et Thibaut Courtois, ont d'ailleurs salué publiquement sa carrière sous sa publication. Une page se tourne pour les Diables Rouges.

En quittant la sélection, Romelu Lukaku laisse un héritage statistique considérable. L'avant-centre se retire en effet en tant que meilleur buteur absolu de l'histoire de la sélection belge avec 94 buts inscrits en 135 sélections. Au niveau des apparitions, le joueur n'est devancé que par Jan Vertonghen (157 sélections) et Axel Witsel (140 sélections). Pilier de la sélection durant plus d'une décennie, il a disputé quatre phases finales de Coupe du monde (2014, 2018 avec une 3e place, 2022 et 2026) ainsi que trois Championnats d'Europe (2016, 2020 et 2024). Son dernier match officiel sous le maillot des Diables Rouges remonte ainsi au 5 octobre 2026 contre l'équipe de France en Ligue des nations, lors d'une défaite (1-4).

Cette annonce constitue d'ailleurs un revirement par rapport aux prepares initialement affichés par l'intéressé. En effet, l'attaquant avait affirmé en janvier 2026 que la Coupe du monde 2026 ne marquerait pas sa dernière compétition majeure avec la Belgique. La sélection des Diables Rouges a elle aussi tenu à rendre hommage à son avant-centre sur son compte officiel X, saluant un joueur qui a écrit un incroyable chapitre de l'histoire de l'équipe nationale.

In a recent development, la situation sportive de l'attaquant s'était toutefois compliquée lors des dernières semaines avec les Diables Rouges. Depuis la prise de fonction de Mark van Bommel comme sélectionneur en août 2026 en remplacement de Rudi Garcia, Romelu Lukaku a vu son temps de jeu diminuer au profit de Charles De Ketelaere. Resté sur le banc lors du récent succès face à l'Italie, le joueur a finalement choisi de renoncer aux prochaines échéances internationales de son pays. En effet, la Belgique disputera les quarts de finale de la Ligue des nations du 25 au 30 mars 2027, dont le tirage au sort est fixé au vendredi 20 novembre 2026 à Nyon.

Industry observers note that toutefois, cette retraite internationale ne met absolument pas un terme à sa carrière en club. Romelu Lukaku évolue sous les couleurs de Fenerbahçe depuis le mois d'août 2026 et reste concentré sur ses objectifs en Turquie. L'attaquant disputera ainsi son prochain match officiel le samedi 21 novembre 2026 à 17h00 face à Kocaelispor en Süper Lig.

Iraola fumes at bungling fourth official for costing Liverpool a penalty

📅 29 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 21 min read (4137 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Andoni Iraola wanted to talk about his team and their need to improve but how could he concentrate on something so straightforward when he had seen something so bizarre?
  • It is important, first and foremost, to explain this is not painting a narrative about Liverpool being unfortunate.
  • Industry observers note that but the penalty that changed the contest?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Andoni Iraola wanted to talk about his team and their need to improve but how could he concentrate on something so straightforward when he had seen something so bizarre?

It is important, first and foremost, to explain this is not painting a narrative about Liverpool being unfortunate. Far from it. Iraola hissed his dismay that Nottingham Forest had shown more intensity and been the better team for long periods in an entertaining 2-2 draw.

Industry observers note that but the penalty that changed the contest? Iraola, his coaching staff, even the supporters behind the dugout had been left flabbergasted that the malfunctioning number board of fourth official Tim Robinson presented an avenue for Forest to exploit.

Iraola had tried to make a triple change, wanting to introduce Ryan Gravenberch, Kostas Tsimikas and Rio Ngumoha, but as Robinson pressed buttons to no avail and everyone in Red became frustrated, Forest substitute Liam Delap took a quick throw and the Liverpool house almost caved in.

Neco Williams, once of Liverpool, surged into the penalty area, Alisson Becker arrived a fraction too late after the defender got his shot away and took his old team-mate down. Morgan Gibbs-White exacerbated the damage when sending Alisson the wrong way and this was the last thing a manager wanting to make an impression on a substantial day needed to see but this was reality.

Recent findings suggest that alisson takes out Neco Williams and Forest have a penalty! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fX2flY3Tob.

It has been revealed that gibbs-White converts from the spot to restore Forest's lead! 🌳🎯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/jeoPiXPArw.

According to recent reports, “I cannot explain because I don’t have an explanation,” Iraola mentioned. “I wanted to make those substitutions about three minutes before. I mean, it was two, three, four times the ball had gone out. I still don’t know the reason why we couldn’t make the subs.

“I think [the fourth official] was having some problems with the board or something. It [the penalty] wouldn’t have happened if I had made the sub. I asked. I had complained the previous time. The supporters were shouting and they were aware of the situation. But I don’t know what happened and I don’t know why they have given the penalty.”.

"A professional fourth official cannot take three minutes." 😳Andoni Iraola was not happy with the time taken to get the substitutes' board ready.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fMfYOjQJPd.

In a recent development, he did know, though, why Liverpool had needed to drag themselves off the deck again for the second week in a row. Iraola has shown in his opening weeks on Merseyside that he is not someone who seeks excuses.

“A lack of intensity hurt us,” Iraola said with obvious disdain and it was only down to a show of character in the second period that a slovenly first half did not enable Forest to win at Anfield for the third consecutive year, for all that the travelling fans thought it was “happening again!”.

According to recent reports, forest, bruised after two defeats in four days to Leeds, looked like an Oliver Glasner side. They were aggressive and well organised, the only failing was that physically they could not see the job through, but the Austrian insisted that will change in due course.

Once Glasner is settled in and he gets his transfer business done – “definitely one, possibly two and probably three,” was his mischievous reply to how the window will unfold – Forest will be a formidable proposition, especially if the first 45 minutes are a barometer.

They had been knocking on the door before Dan Ndoye eventually broke the deadlock, sweeping a left-footed drive past Alisson after Igor Jesus had won a header from a long clearance. It was a simple goal, marginally onside, but it was absolutely deserved.

Ndoye gives Forest the lead at Anfield! 🌳🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ag0oZ7UjTm.

In a recent development, “There were many positive aspects,” stated Glasner. “It has been a three-game week; some players played. We are getting more and more fitness, that is just the foundation of how we want to play. It is just a point but it still feels a bit frustrating, so we have to stay humble.”.

"I think we were very poor in the first half." 😤Andoni Iraola gives his assessment of Liverpool's performance against Nottingham Forest.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/COZfhwkLeX.

Neco Williams and James McAtee react to Nottingham Forest's draw at Anfield 🌳🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BjX0p1yQ1m.

"We started the game pretty bad today." 😬Alexander Isak gives his assessment of Liverpool's performance at Anfield.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/3wD0hplmQ6.

The playmaker added another goal and assist to his tally this afternoon.

Industry observers note that 20 - Morgan Gibbs-White has been directly involved in 20 goals in 2026 (15 goals, 5 assists), the joint-most of any Premier League player in all competitions (level with Haaland).His 13 goals in the Premier League in 2026 are also the most of any player.Decisive. pic.twitter.com/p1wQFwXvsI.

Liverpool and Forest are both made to wait for their first Premier League wins of the season as the two sides play out a pulsating 2-2 draw at Anfield.

Full-time scenes at Anfield as Liverpool and Nottingham Forest share the points 🤝📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/WqOpfU38es.

It has been revealed that sels calmly comes out to claim a deep cross to relieve the pressure on Forest. Munoz runs back to dispossess Delap and win a free kick, giving Liverpool another chance to launch the ball forward.

Glasner makes a very late double change as Hudson-Odoi and Dominguez replace McAtee and Igor Jesus.

In a recent development, there will be five minutes of added time. Liverpool continue their relentless search for a third goal, while Forest are holding on.

It’s wave after wave of Liverpool pressure. Forest are camped inside their own half. Igor Jesus and Delap are chasing every loose ball, but Forest are struggling to get out at the moment.

Industry observers note that munoz’s goal has provided another twist in this pulsating encounter. Isak wins a free kick in such dangerous territory and Szoboszlai steps up to take it. The Hungarian slams a venomous effort wide of the far post. Can either side find a late winner?

Sources indicate that what an incredible finish! Wirtz threads a delightful pass through to Munoz. With his back to goal, the winger swivels and takes the ball on the outside of Murillo, before smashing a thunderous effort into the roof of the net, which brushes the crossbar on its way in.

Munoz, take a bow! 🤯👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/GD8IAdy2rJ.

Igor Jesus does brilliantly to escape Nyoni, before he is pulled to the ground by Arajou, who is booked. It’s been an excellent defensive effort from Forest.

Recent findings suggest that iraola makes his final two alterations as Araujo and Nyoni replace Jacquet and Mac Allister. Szoboszlai then swings such an inviting delivery into the penalty area, but Isak miscues his strike with his left foot.

Amid the chaos, Alisson was booked just before the penalty after appealing the decision and Iraola has ordered a triple change, taking off Kerkez, Frimpong and Gakpo for Tsimikas, Gravenberch and Ngumoha. This has seen Szoboszlai move out to right back.

According to recent reports, andoni Iraola is about to make his substitution and this is interesting because he had planned to introduce Rio Ngumoha, Kostas Tsimikas and Ryan Gravenberch 10 minutes ago but told them to sit down after Liverpool had equalised. Forest have put Liam Delap on, giving him his debut after completing his £45m move to the club.

Sources indicate that the Forest captain sends Alisson the wrong way, powering a clinical penalty into the net. Gibbs-White demonstrates fantastic composure and Liverpool have it all to do again.

Gibbs-White converts from the spot to restore Forest's lead! 🌳🎯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/jeoPiXPArw.

Delap showcases excellent initiative and takes a quick throw-in to send Williams through on goal. Alisson rushes out and catches Williams as he attempts to lob the goalkeeper. Williams crashes to the ground and the referee points to the spot. Alisson is furious. What a chance for Forest to restore their lead.

Alisson takes out Neco Williams and Forest have a penalty! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fX2flY3Tob.

This game is being played at a ferocious pace and Forest’s club-record signing Delap enters the action as he replaces Ndoye. Can the former Chelsea striker mark his debut with a much-needed goal?

That leveller has injected so much energy into Liverpool. Anfield believes again. Isak really needed that goal.

Recent findings suggest that so much credit must go to Gakpo. The winger shrugs off Williams and fires a pinpoint cross towards the back post. Isak is there and converts from close range. We’re set up for such an intriguing finale. Liverpool have the momentum now.

Isak equalises for Liverpool at the Kop end! 🔴🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/qKFxq2AqaB.

Recent findings suggest that wirtz’s frustrating afternoon is compounded as he picks up a booking after hauling Murillo to the ground. Iraola looks to be readying some substitutions.

There is a very strange feeling here: it’s almost a case of the home fans waiting for Nottingham Forest to score a second goal rather than anticipating that Liverpool will equalise. The early buzz in the atmosphere has gone and that is because the gaps everyone can see in the make up of the team remain. How Bradley Barcola will transform this situation?

Sources indicate that jacquet’s pass is intercepted and Ndoye is released on the counter. He’s guided out wide by Van Dijk but still squeezes in a brilliant cross. Gibbs-White was running up the pitch in support and slowed down, meaning no one was there to turn in Ndoye’s delivery.

Munoz is the next player to be booked after reacting angrily to a decision. Iraola has to consider making some changes soon.

Aina catches Munoz with a late challenge and he’s the second Forest player to go into the referee’s book.

In a recent development, you can already see in this second half that there is acres of space for Forest to exploit on the counter as Liverpool push for a leveller. Munoz then heads a point-blank header over the bar. Luckily for the Spaniard, the offside flag was up against Gakpo.

Recent findings suggest that we are back for the second half here at Anfield. Can Liverpool find a route back into this game or can Forest hold onto the three points?

It’s a bizarre situation for Liverpool. They could easily be level or be 2-0 down. But they trial just 1-0 at half-time. Wirtz and Gakpo are looking lively, but Isak has struggled to influence the game.

Dan Ndoye scores his first goal in the Premier League in 377 days 🤯 pic.twitter.com/tjSiGoSPyW.

Recent findings suggest that forest have a slender one-goal advantage at the break after a frantic first half at Anfield. Ndoye curled the visitors into a well-deserved lead after 24 minutes, before Wirtz had a goal ruled out for offside. The German was then sensationally denied by Sels’ diving save as he tipped Wirtz’s header over the bar. Alisson then replicated Sels’ heroics, parrying Igor Jesus’ strike against the woodwork to stop Forest from doubling their lead.

What a move and what a save! Murillo sprays an inch-perfect pass out to Aina, who chops inside of Munoz and fires a low cross into Igor Jesus. The Forest striker shoots first-time from inside the penalty area, but his effort is sensationally parried onto the bar by Alisson. That is a world-class stop from the Brazilian goalkeeper.

It has been revealed that A world-class save from Alisson denies Forest a second! 🤯🧤📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/4NtzROILrU.

Igor Jesus receives the game’s first yellow card after clipping Mac Allister with an unnecessary challenge.

Sources indicate that liverpool then fly forward again as Gakpo nutmegs Williams. His cross trickles through to Munoz at the back post. The ball is slightly behind Munoz and he leans back before shooting, causing his strike to narrowly sail over the bar.

There will be three minutes of added time to conclude this first half.

Recent findings suggest that liverpool are applying all the pressure at the end of this first half. At times, Forest have had every outfield player behind the ball.

Sels makes a superb save! Gakpo takes on his marker on the outside and fires in a cross which Wirtz meets. The attacker gets in between Schlager and Aina to win the header, but his effort is excellently tipped over the bar by Sels.

Out of nothing, Liverpool are level. McAtee attempts to play out from a deep position and his pass is intercepted by Wirtz. The ball breaks to Frimpong, who slips a clever pass to Wirtz. The German playmaker swivels and slides a low effort into the bottom corner. It’s a brilliant finish, but Frimpong was in an offside position before he provided the assist. VAR confirms this and Liverpool’s joy has been cut short. That is a huge let off for Forest, who need to be more careful with possession in deeper areas.

Following that Forest goal, there was a small flurry of Liverpool pressure, with Szoboszlai having a free kick punched away by Sels. Murillo is then very careless with the ball and is dispossessed. This allowed Mac Allister to play in Isak, but the striker is crowded out by multiple Forest defenders before he can get a shot away.

For the third season in a row, Nottingham Forest lead at Anfield. The goal had been coming, too. Liverpool were bright early but suddenly massive gaps have started appearing and Forest are wily enough to exploit. There are lots of gripes around the stands about it being “too easy” and this knowledgeable crowd are right. A long ball forward and a simple flick has caused mayhem.

According to recent reports, forest are ahead and are well worth their lead. Sels rolls out a long ball up to Igor Jesus, who takes it down with an exquisite touch. The ball then breaks to Gibbs-White. The Forest captain plays in Ndoye and the winger curls a clinical effort into the far bottom corner to send the away support wild.

Ndoye gives Forest the lead at Anfield! 🌳🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ag0oZ7UjTm.

Huge chance for Forest! McAtee drops deep and picks out Ndoye with a teasing cross. The forward meets the delivery and his header bounces wide. Upon the replays, there looks to have been a push on Frimpong by Ndoye. The referee’s whistle wasn’t sounded so it would have been interesting to see what would of happened if that chance had been converted.

Industry observers note that it’s been a really frantic start to this game. Out of possession, Forest are retreating into a really rigid back five formation. Going forward, Aina and Williams are getting up the pitch at every opportunity.

Aina stands up an inviting cross to the back post for Ndoye, who heads it back into the danger zone. Igor Jesus latches onto it, but Jacquet makes a goal-saving tackle to block the striker’s close-range effort.

Sensational block from Jeremy Jacquet to deny Igor Jesus! 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/XuhO1GuE9F.

There’s a shoulder-to-shoulder, and the Forest defender bumps Isak off the ball, before Milenkovic comes back to mop up the danger.

Ndoye attempts to sprint in behind Liverpool’s defence. He’s chased by Jacquet and Ndoye can’t quite take the ball under his spell. That is an early warning sign for Liverpool.

The hosts then go up the other end as Mac Allister threads a delightful pass through to Gakpo. The Liverpool forward tries to swivel and shoot, but Williams tracks back and makes a crucial tackle.

Industry observers note that frimpong gets in behind Forest’s backline and attempts to pick out Gakpo with a cross aimed towards the back post. However, the ball bobbles and the Liverpool right back overhits his delivery.

A very intriguing team selected by Andoni Iraola and one that illustrates his confidence. It could be viewed as significant call to drop Ryan Gravenberch and Rio Ngumoha but Victor Munoz and Alexis Mac Allister both made a difference when they were introduced at St James’s Park last Sunday and they warrant their inclusion. Munoz won’t be fit enough to play 90 minutes but it will be fascinating to watch him, particularly as Bradley Barcola will soon arrive to play in the same position on the left flank.

We are now under way at Anfield. Can Iraola mark his first competitive home game with a win or will Glasner get up and running with Forest?

The substantial story with Forest will come later, with their pursuit of Everton’s Harrison Armstrong. It it is a transfer that is causing huge discussion on Merseyside.

Both sets of players are out onto the pitch and are met by an electric atmosphere at Anfield.

Earlier this month, Liverpool owners Fenway Sports Group confirmed they had agreed to sell a minority equity stake to 1892 Holdings, a consortium led and managed by Amit Bhatia, who is in attendance at Anfield today.

Industry observers note that on the development, Bhatia told Liverpool’s website: “It feels incredible. It feels surreal when I hear those words, obviously an incredibly proud moment for myself, for my family, for our partners. We’re talking about Liverpool Football Club here, right? I mean, we’re talking about the greatest football club in the world. And so to have the ability to be involved in any capacity is a huge privilege and a huge honour.”.

Having been linked to both Tottenham Hotspur and Manchester City, Cody Gakpo’s Liverpool future has looked doubtful at points this summer.

However, Spurs’ signings of Savinho and Omar Marmoush, as well as Manchester City’s potentially big-money pursuit of Enzo Fernandez, means that any exit for the Dutchman looks extremely complicated.

Gakpo scored Liverpool’s first equaliser in their chaotic 2-2 draw with Newcastle United and starts today on the left wing.

❤️ https://t.co/MgbTcQWank pic.twitter.com/DwIooN2OFk.

In September 2024, Nottingham Forest claimed their first win over Liverpool at Anfield in 55 years thanks to Callum Hudson-Odoi’s sumptuous 72nd-minute curler.

When Callum Hudson-Odoi made history at Anfield 🤩 pic.twitter.com/HhJ73WztMd.

Last season’s emphatic 3-0 victory in the same fixture under Sean Dyche means that Forest have successive wins at a ground where they could notoriously never manage three points.

Nottingham Forest have smashed their club-record transfer fee to sign Chelsea striker Liam Delap for £50m on a five-year deal, ending a lengthy pursuit by both the club and their head coach Oliver Glasner.

Last summer Delap held talks with Forest and Glasner, while he was in charge at Crystal Palace, before he opted to join his mentor and former Manchester City Under-21 coach Enzo Maresca at Stamford Bridge.

One of the summer’s most talked about and protracted transfer pursuits is nearing its conclusion as Liverpool have agreed a £120m deal with Paris St-Germain to sign Bradley Barcola.

The Frenchman was absent from PSG’s squad on Friday evening as Luis Enrique’s side drew 2-2 with Lille in Ligue 1.

Barcola is yet another big-money addition to Liverpool’s forward line, following on from the signings of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Hugo Ekitike last summer.

He also has the approval of club legend Steven Gerrard, who is at Anfield on duty for TNT Sports.

Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League match between Liverpool and Nottingham Forest at Anfield.

This encounter pits two summer appointments – Andoni Iraola and Oliver Glasner – against each other as they both search for their first top-flight win at their latest clubs.

In a recent development, in the opening Premier League game-week, Iraola’s Liverpool needed a last-gasp 99th-minute penalty from Dominik Szoboszlai to rescue an unconvincing 2-2 draw with Newcastle United at St. James’ Park. Meanwhile, Nottingham Forest have suffered back-to-back home defeats in four days against Leeds United without scoring (1-0 Premier League, 2-0 Carabao Cup).

Iraola has been handed the unenviable task of steering Liverpool back on track following a hugely disappointing campaign under Arne Slot, whose side’s defence of their Premier League ended in a meek fifth-place finish despite spending more than £400m in the previous summer.

The former Bournemouth boss must uncover how to get the best out of big-money recruits such as Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Milos Kerkez and Jeremie Frimpong, and also tighten up Liverpool’s vulnerable midfield and defence. Given the pressure of the job and the club’s hectic schedule while balancing domestic and European football, it’s a tough ask. However, Liverpool have agreed a £120m deal for Paris St-Germain winger Bradley Barcola to bolster their attacking reinforcements, but the transfer hasn’t been finalised in time for today’s match.

Last season, Forest endured an equally tumultuous campaign, churning through a staggering four managers, before eventually stumbling to a 16th-place finish. Glasner has been hand-picked by owner Evangelos Marinakis to usher in an era of stability and success, after winning the FA Cup, Community Shield and Conference League in just over two years at Crystal Palace.

Both Marinakis and Glasner are extremely ambitious and demanding figures. You’d imagine a top-half finish would be considered the absolute minimum for Forest, while Glasner’s track record of winning trophies surely indicates that Marinakis is eyeing some silverware at the City Ground.

Recent findings suggest that it’s a meeting of two managers who must deliver. Three points for either side would serve as a much-needed tonic to kickstart their seasons.

Kick-off is at 12:30, with team news coming shortly.

It has been revealed that ce début d'exercice s'avère particulièrement difficile pour le joueur de 26 ans sous les couleurs du club espagnol. Un rendement bien loin de ses standards. La cause de ce passage à vide trouve son origine dans les suites de la Coupe du monde, où le Brésil a quitté la compétition dès les huitièmes de finale après une défaite face à la Norvège (2-1). Très affecté par ce revers, l'attaquant a ainsi privilégié le repos et la déconnexion en famille durant ses vacances, au détriment de sa préparation physique.

Devant les médias à Singapour, l'ailier madrilène a d'ailleurs détaillé avec franchise les raisons de ce déficit athlétique :.

L'attaquant a ainsi reconnu que ces remous avaient directement influé sur son niveau de jeu depuis la reprise.

Toutefois, l'ailier madrilène a tenu à rappeler la difficulté de se maintenir au sommet dans la durée. Pour appuyer son constat, il a souligné que seuls Cristiano Ronaldo et Lionel Messi ont su afficher de telles statistiques pendant de longues années. Le numéro 7 brésilien a également rappelé son devoir d'exemplarité, affirmant être conscient que s'il court davantage, tous les jeunes joueurs courront aussi plus.

Vinicius Jr a tempéré les inquiétudes en comparant sa trajectoire à celle de la saison passée, où il ne comptait que 5 buts en décembre avant de dépasser la barre des 20 réalisations au printemps. L'attaquant reste ainsi convaincu que sa montée en puissance physique portera ses fruits au moment opportun.

According to recent reports, sur le blueprint sportif en sélection, Vinicius Jr s'est d'ailleurs redonné de la confiance en signant un doublé samedi 14 novembre 2026 lors de la défaite du Brésil contre le Japon (2-3) au Stade national de Singapour. Le prochain rendez-vous de Vinicius Jr avec le Real Madrid est ensuite programmé le samedi 21 novembre 2026 à 21h00 face au Celta Vigo au stade Santiago-Bernabéu pour la 13e journée de Liga.

Latest Update: £380m = zero points: Substantial-spending Spurs humbled by Newcastle

💡 Key Takeaways
  • These remain the earliest of early days but the blunt facts are there for all to see.
  • It has been revealed that not since 1974 has a Spurs team lost the first two games of a league campaign without finding the net.
  • This meeting with Newcastle United was, in the minds of those Spurs fans, meant to be a clash between a team remade by the transfer market and a team broken by it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

These remain the earliest of early days but the blunt facts are there for all to see. Tottenham Hotspur, the club that has spent around £380m this summer in search of instant improvements, have played twice and lost twice in the Premier League. After making eight new signings, they have so far scored zero goals and won zero points.

It has been revealed that not since 1974 has a Spurs team lost the first two games of a league campaign without finding the net. The summer enthusiasm in this corner of north London is therefore already drifting away, to the sound of an alarmingly familiar soundtrack: boos from the home supporters at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

This meeting with Newcastle United was, in the minds of those Spurs fans, meant to be a clash between a team remade by the transfer market and a team broken by it. Yet it was Newcastle, still adjusting to the loss of three key players this summer, who looked the more unified group and more organised team.

Industry observers note that it proved to be a truly glorious evening for the visiting supporters, who not only delighted in their team’s victory but also in the struggles of Sandro Tonali. The £100m Italian, who swapped Newcastle for Spurs a few weeks ago, never came close to offering the sort of class one would expect for such a fee. That price tag is not his fault but it is his burden, and in time he will need to shoulder it more impressively than he did here.

It has been revealed that roberto De Zerbi, the Spurs head coach, can rightly say that it will take time for his newly introduced group to develop the cohesion he needs. The worrying reality for Spurs, though, is that his opposite number had far less time to work with his players and far less money to reshape his squad. Matthias Jaissle appears to be a man with a defined initiative, and an ability to convey it. Newcastle improved considerably after half-time, which spoke volumes of Jaissle’s work. “He is the best signing of Newcastle so far,” noted Yoane Wissa of his new coach.

"He is the best signing for Newcastle"Yoane Wissa praises Matthias Jaissle's impact at the club since becoming head coach 👔 pic.twitter.com/dX8nVknpKc.

For Spurs, so much of it would have felt painfully similar to last season, when they won only three home games in the Premier League. They played some pretty football in bursts, but not at the crucial points of the game. The second half, especially, was pockmarked with moments of despair. There was Mathys Tel’s free-kick that almost flew into Islington, for example, and Mateus Fernandes falling over when running onto a pass in the penalty area.

De Zerbi said he was sorry for the fans and for the club, and suggested his team is not properly prepared for this campaign. “Maybe we are not ready yet,” he said. “For many, many reasons we are not ready yet.”.

"I have no panic, I know very well where I'm going" Roberto De Zerbi apologises to Spurs fans after the defeat to Newcastle 🔊 pic.twitter.com/83DntjG5ZH.

It has been revealed that newcastle’s two goals, much like Brentford’s three last weekend, exposed the enduring frailties in the Spurs defence. Anthony Elanga’s opener stemmed from a long pass over the top of the home side’s high line, while Wissa’s acrobatic effort came from a corner kick that Spurs could not handle. Neither strike, it would be safe to say, was the result of world-class attacking play.

Anthony Elanga finishes brilliantly and celebrates just as Thierry Henry did against Spurs 💥 pic.twitter.com/l6qndlMrKm.

Sources indicate that what a GOAL from Yoane Wissa?! 🫨 pic.twitter.com/mjuHpaa4YY.

“After the first goal we lost confidence,” said De Zerbi. “The reaction was not good enough, not what I want to see on the pitch. The solution is not to put the head down, but to react.”.

Sources indicate that to be clear, Spurs were not quite as bad as they had been against Brentford on the opening day. They did create chances here, taking 17 shots and forcing a few terrific saves from Lukas Hornicek, Newcastle’s impressive goalkeeper. But in the key moments they suffered from the same absence of clarity and execution as they did last season. Troublingly, this seemed to affect the newly introduced signings as much as it did the longer-serving players.

Of the five latest arrivals who featured for Spurs, Tonali was the least effective. The Italian had been vigorously booed by the away fans before kick-off and the travelling Geordies waited with palpable excitement for his first mistake. Much to their delight, it arrived after only three minutes: an underhit pass, in his own half, which directly led to Micky van de Ven picking up a yellow card. Tonali was outshone by new Newcastle midfielder Nico Gonzalez, who excelled only a few days after completing his move from Manchester City.

"He's got an opportunity to be the main man"Jamie Redknapp praises Nico Gonzalez's performance on his debut 👏 pic.twitter.com/1ga3tsxXHA.

Might it have been different for Spurs if £75m winger Savio had been available? The Brazilian was electrifying on his debut in midweek, when he scored against Charlton Athletic in the League Cup, yet was unavailable here due to a minor injury. It instead fell to another signing from City, Omar Marmoush, to lead the attack. He was busy and floaty but never truly hurt Newcastle.

There are more changes to come at Spurs before Tuesday’s deadline. De Zerbi revealed after the game that Richarlison, Kevin Danso and Pape Matar Sarr have all asked to leave the club.

Recent findings suggest that at least the issues facing his players appear clear to De Zerbi. His list of areas to improve was lengthy – he spoke of strengthening the connection between the players, the quality of their play, their work in the defensive phase and the distances between them – but he also insisted he loves them and remains confident in the club’s project. At this rate, though, the fans might not share that confidence for much longer.

The Tottenham boss told BBC Sport: “Disappointed for the result because until the first goal we conceded I think we played better than Newcastle. We lost ball possession in the first half because we didn’t defend in the right way, the distance between the defenders and attackers was too big. We can improve in the defensive phases but today was an unfair result.

In a recent development, “At the beginning of the second half we had some chance to create the potential chances. We created many chances to score, we have to improve the last decision, because that will make a difference. At the end we are disappointed for the result and our fans. We are working to be a great team. When we become a team I think we can change the story of the last two seasons for Tottenham.

“We are working to be good on the pitch, if you believe in work and training then you have to improve day by day.”.

Speaking to Sky Sports, Newcastle’s head coach mentioned: “It was incredible and I’m really proud. We are really proud as a club, as a coaching staff to see a team on the pitch delivering the match strategy at a high level already, but also seeing players fully committed to what we’re doing. This is a good start and a moment to enjoy.

“We also did well last week against Liverpool, therefore it was a step in the right direction again against a strong opponent with huge signings during the transfer window. This is something we were aware of, but how we handled that challenge was amazing.”.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League meeting between Tottenham and Newcastle United in North London.

Following consecutive 17th-place finishes in the last two seasons, Spurs are looking to enjoy a fresh start under Roberto De Zerbi without nervously looking over their shoulder at the perilous possibility of relegation.

Nevertheless, Spurs’ season started disastrously last weekend as they fell to a miserable 3-0 defeat against Brentford at the Gtech Community Stadium. Since that result, Spurs have responded with an emphatic 5-1 thrashing of Charlton Athletic in the Carabao Cup, and also confirmed the signings of Savinho and Omar Marmoush from Manchester City. De Zerbi will be looking to continue this newfound momentum in the club’s first top-flight home match of the 2026-27 campaign.

Industry observers note that newcastle United have undergone a summer of significant change. Eddie Howe stepped down as head coach after nearly five years in charge, while Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon all departed the club for lucrative transfer fees. Tonali welcomes his former employers to his new surroundings after joining Tottenham for £100m.

In a recent development, despite this upheaval, Newcastle demonstrated admirable heart in new boss Matthias Jaissle’s first game in charge, earning a hard-fought 2-2 draw with Liverpool at St. James’ Park on the opening weekend. Emotional tributes poured in for club legend Kevin Keegan as Alexander Isak made his return to the club he acrimoniously forced an exit from last summer.

According to recent reports, newcastle looked to be heading for a victory after goals from Anthony Elanga and Joe Willock, until Lewis Hall, who had played excellently, apprehended Liverpool substitute Victor Munoz in added time to concede a penalty. Dominik Szoboszlai smashed a clinical spot-kick into the top corner to rescue a point for the visitors. Newcastle bounced back from these dropped points with a tense 3-2 triumph over West Brom in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday evening.

A first Premier League win of the season is the aim for both clubs by the end of this evening.

Kick-off is at 17:30, with team news on the way shortly.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A prominent former Premier League referee has questioned the selection of officiasl for the fixture between Liverpool and Manchester United at Anfield on Sunday.

Recent findings suggest that as confirmed via premierleague.com, Sam Barrott will take charge of the match, with Adam Nunn and Lee Betts as his assistants, while Chris Kavanagh is fourth official. John Brooks is on VAR, assisted by Paul Howard.

The upcoming game is the Reds’ sixth home match in the top flight this season, and it’ll be the third to have had the Yorkshire native as the referee.

Upon learning that curious fact, Keith Hackett took to social media to endorse Barrott as a referee but question the decision-making process which has led to him being dispatched to Anfield once again.

The former chief executive of the PGMOL (now Pro Ref) posted on X: ‘A top-class referee, but not a very good appointing procedure by his bosses’.

According to recent reports, want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

It’s a strong show of faith by Pro Ref chief executive Howard Webb to assign Barrott to what is always the most high-profile fixture in English football, and arguably world football.

Liverpool fans might be forgiven for not being able to summon much enthusiasm over the appointment, given the official’s previous at Anfield this season.

In a recent development, in August, it was he who awarded Nottingham Forest a penalty in their 2-2 draw against the Reds when Neco Williams went to ground under a challenge from Alisson Becker. The Premier League’s Key Match Incidents Panel subsequently adjudged that the spot kick was wrongly given.

While there are clear critera which must be observed when appointing match officials to specific fixtures – any officials from Merseyside or Manchester are obviously ineligible for Sunday’s clash at Anfield – seeing Barrott assigned to yet another Liverpool home game does seem anomalous.

We just hope – for his sake as much as anyone else’s – that the main talking point after the final whistle isn’t a controversial and decisive error on his part. The last thing we need is yet more dubious refereeeing affecting the Reds.

Welcome to our Live Comments section, where latest comments will appear automatically.

Howard Webb does this on purpose, him being United’s 12th man in these fixtures previously. He was always controversial in his decisions, so you can guarantee that will be the case come Sunday, with Barrott being a very poor choice by Webb.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool are ready to let a long-serving stalwart leave Anfield for free in 2027, according to one insider.

The last player standing from the tail end of Brendan Rodgers’ managerial reign, Joe Gomez is now into his 12th season with the Reds, albeit that he’s been consigned to a backup role thus far under Andoni Iraola.

The 29-year-old has featured for just 259 minutes across our 16 matches so far in this campaign, more than half of which have come in the Carabao Cup (Transfermarkt), and as it stand he’ll be out of contract in seven months’ time.

Ex-Manchester United chief scout Mick Brown has claimed that Liverpool sporting director Julian Ward has already decided that the club’s longest-serving current player won’t be offered a new deal, with injury concerns not helping the defender’s case.

He told Football Insider: “Liverpool have already decided they’re going to let Joe Gomez leave. He doesn’t have much of a role to play at the moment, he’s not starting games at right-back even despite their injuries, and he isn’t competing for a centre-back position.

Industry observers note that “His injuries are always a concern as well. They don’t think he can start games consistently, and all of these challenges stack up eventually.

“It would be a surprise to me if they were to offer him a fresh contract, especially when you consider they’re going to be looking to bring in new defenders at some stage.

“If he hasn’t played much this season, that’s not going to change with fresh players coming in, so I expect he’ll be allowed to look at what other options might be available.”.

It has been revealed that want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Ward could be quite busy with contract renewals over the next few months, with Alisson Becker, Virgil van Dijk and Alexis Mac Allister reportedly all in line for prospective fresh deals.

Whereas that trio are virtually guaranteed to start, though, Gomez usually has to rely on substitute appearances or heavy squad rotation for domestic cup games, and it’s not implausible that he could be allowed to depart on a free transfer next summer.

If that is indeed his fate, he’ll be assured of a raucous send-off at Anfield on the final day of the season, with his popularity among the fan base unmistakably evident by the roar which greeted his successful penalty in the Carabao Cup shootout triumph over Chelsea last month.

As Lewis Steele rightly said, the 29-year-old ‘very rarely puts a foot wrong’ whenever he’s called upon, and even if he isn’t getting much game-time, we don’t doubt that he’s imparting some invaluable advice to the young defenders at Liverpool who can learn so much from him.

According to recent reports, if this is to be Gomez’s last campaign with the Reds, all we ask is that he does finally, finally get his first goal for the club during regulation time. You’d be very hard pressed to find a more popular goalscorer if that moment were to happen!

FEATURE | Five things we learned from Bundesliga Matchday 10

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (907 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Getfootballnewsgermany

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the Bundesliga returned following the final international break of the year, and what a spectacle it was.
  • This would seem like an obvious thing to say after Harry Kane was ruled out for the next three months with an ankle injury,, while Luis Diaz, Ismael Saibari and Serge Gnabry are also out injured, but this has been a problem for most of the season too, and these injuries are likely to make the matter worse.
  • Even with Kane fit, Bayern have been wasteful in front of goal this season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the Bundesliga returned following the final international break of the year, and what a spectacle it was. From a swing of the title race pendulum, to changes at the bottom of the table, Get German Football News has you covered with the latest talking points after Matchday 10.

Here are five things we learned….

This would seem like an obvious thing to say after Harry Kane was ruled out for the next three months with an ankle injury,, while Luis Diaz, Ismael Saibari and Serge Gnabry are also out injured, but this has been a problem for most of the season too, and these injuries are likely to make the matter worse.

Even with Kane fit, Bayern have been wasteful in front of goal this season. Granted, some of the results the ball just wouldn’t go in, like against Schalke and Augsburg, but the difference between this season and last year was that Bayern would prove to be far more clinical in front of goal, but Germany’s record champions seemed to have lost that edge now, as shown in their 1-1 draw with Cologne on Friday night.

This has resulted in games where Bayern should win comfortably being a lot more difficult, mainly due to their own doing. With the injury to Kane, and with no fit back-up, this problem is likely to get worse and could make or break Bayern’s Bundesliga season. It’s now up to Vincent Kompany and his coaching team to find a solution, and quick.

According to recent reports, usually after Bayern drop points, Dortmund fail to capitalise, and ultimately, nothing would change. However, Matchday 10 was different.

According to recent reports, naturally, Dortmund did not make it easy for themselves against last-placed Borussia Mönchengladbach as they struggled to break down Alexander Blessin’s side, while Felix Nmecha’s winner in the 80th minute came from a mistake by Gladbach keeper Daniel Batz. But a win is a win, and Dortmund are now top of the Bundesliga with a two-point lead over Bayern.

Considering how this has been a problem for Dortmund before, it goes to show the effect that Niko Kovač is having on the side, that they are able to win these types of games – and to win ugly, especially when they have previously struggled in the past. Their latest 1-0 victory is already the third of its kind this season.

We probably now have a title race on our hands.

While the move is still technically a loan, it is more than likely that RB Leipzig will make the signing of Brajan Gruda permanent, and they will have to do their best not to immediately flip him for what will be a healthy profit.

Since returning to Leipzig in the summer, Gruda has been one of Leipzig’s standout players, like Antonio Nusa and Christopher Nkunku. The 22-year-old only made his Germany debut in the recent international break, but he immediately hit the ground running under Jürgen Klopp – where he recorded two goals and provided two assists against Serbia and the Netherlands – while also continuing his Bundesliga form.

It has been revealed that the winger scored his first Bundesliga goal of the season in Leipzig’s 5-1 rout against Union Berlin, while also providing the assist for Leipzig’s second goal of the day. In the opening stages of the season, it looked as if Leipzig were missing Yan Diomande, but Gruda has replaced the now Real Madrid player with relative ease.

Sources indicate that while, on paper, a 0-0 draw against UEFA Champions League participants VfB Stuttgart is a good result, fans will certainly feel uneasy at their precarious position in the Bundesliga. The Royal Blues’ draw and Union Berlin’s 5-1 defeat against RB Leipzig sees Miron Muslic’s charges climb into the promotion/relegation play-off, but the fact that they are yet to score at the Veltins Arena is a worrying one.

No team has scored fewer than their five goals in ten games this season and with games against fellow Bundesliga returnees Paderborn, Revierderby rivals Borussia Dortmund, Hamburg and Borussia Mönchengladbach, it’s difficult to see where goals will arrive from.

Industry observers note that after a 4-1 defeat against Freiburg on Matchday 1, few gave Werder Bremen little chance of remaining in the division this season, especially given the departures of Mio Backhaus and Romano Schmid, long-term injury to Jens Stage, and being somewhat light up top. But, the impressive team cohesion intertwined with Niclas Füllkrug’s timely return has made the Green-Whites incredibly fun to watch.

Füllkrug struck his tenth Bundesliga goal of the season, and Bremen’s fourth against Hamburg in the Bundesliga’s 111th Nordderby, as Daniel Thioune’s charges secured bragging rights over their northern rivals – a timely present for the head coach that had just signed a contract extension.

Recent findings suggest that sitting sixth, Bremen have turned the Weserstadion into a fortress, where they remain unbeaten with four wins and a draw in the Bundesliga this season, which places them three points clear of chasing Eintracht Frankfurt. While free-scoring RB Leipzig and well-ran Freiburg are deservedly in the top four, they’ll be rightly looking in their rear view mirror to see Bremen hunting them down.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hungary manager Marco Rossi has defended his usage of Dominik Szoboszlai during this international window.

The Liverpool midfielder sprained his knee during the Reds’ 3-1 victory at Crystal Palace the weekend before last and admitted that he nearly pulled out of his country’s win over Georgia six days later.

His choice to represent his nation was condemned by some reporters back on Merseyside, amid fears of aggravating the injury and compromising his involvement for his club over the coming weeks as the fixtures come thick and fast for Andoni Iraola’s side.

Rossi was defiant when quizzed about Szoboszlai ahead of Hungary’s match against Northern Ireland on Tuesday night.

In a recent development, he told reporters (via Origo Sport): “Did you see any problems with Dominik in the Georgia game? Because I didn’t see any. He played like he usually does, so there are no problems from our side. He notes he’s ready, he’s available, so he’ll play.”.

The Hungary boss was true to his word, as the Liverpool star played the entirety of the Northern Ireland game, thankfully seeming to come through it without any adverse effects.

Recent findings suggest that want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

We can understand Szoboszlai wanting to represent his country, especially in his role as captain, but those who pay his wages at Anfield mightn’t have been overly impressed with his decision to play on despite knowing prior to the Georgia match that he wasn’t operating at 100%.

That Liverpool don’t play until Sunday at 4:30pm gives the 26-year-old that bit of additional time to manage his fitness carefully so that he’s in prime condition for the game against Manchester United.

Whether or not the midfielder will start that match is debatable. The in-form Alexis Mac Allister and Florian Wirtz will likely have two of the three midfield berths nailed down, and the excellent displays of Trey Nyoni have made it difficult to omit him from the XI.

Also, if Iraola feels that Szoboszlai isn’t fully fit by Sunday, he probably won’t take the risk of throwing our number 8 back into the starting line-up, instead keeping him in reserve should he be needed off the bench.

Hopefully the influential Hungarian won’t suffer any further complications over the next four days, and everyone associated with Liverpool will surely be glad that the international window is out of the way, with the next one not upon us until late March 2027.

Borussia Mönchengladbach star Wael Mohya is attracting interest from several big clubs, including Bayern Munich, and was subsequently named in Jürgen Klopp’s 24-man squad for the November international break, but the 17-year-old isn’t for sale.

Speaking about the transfer links on Sky90, Gladbach sporting director Rouven Schröder stated: “He is definitely not for sale in January. And the rest will depend on how the market develops.”.

Mohya has played 10 Bundesliga games for Gladbach this season and has found the net two times while assisting once. He has already matched the tally from last season, in which he made 15 Bundesliga appearances in total. Primarily playing in attacking midfield, he is also capable of playing on either side of the wing.

It has been revealed that regarding the fee the club is looking for, Schröder noted: “We’ve all been in this business for far too long to comment on figures. We’re delighted to have him here. He’s a really, really wonderful kid. He’s a fantastic talent, but he’s still only 17. We shouldn’t forget that.”.

The player, who is valued at €17m by Transfermarkt, has a contract that will keep him at the club until 2028. However, with increased interest in the player, Gladbach could struggle to keep hold of him beyond the summer.

Sources indicate that wirtz is showing his best qualities for the German national team as well. During the last international break, he scored a goal against Serbia and two against the Netherlands.

Recent findings suggest that speaking on whether Wirtz has ‘returned from international duty with more confidence’, Iraola mentioned: “ No, I think he has been playing very well for a long, sustained period of time. He finished before the break with a goal and an assist against Crystal Palace, an assist the game before. He has consistently been playing well for a good period of time. He’s going to maybe continue playing well sometimes without an assist, without a goal, but still, I think he is giving us a lot.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bayern Munich goalkeeper Sven Ulreich stated that he is yet to make a decision about his future.

“I will be speaking with Bayern in the near future about what happens next, what the club wants,” he exclusively told Kicker.

In a recent development, ulreich had been number two behind Manuel Neuer for several years at Bayern before dropping behind Jonas Urbig in the pecking order. With the likely situation that the World Cup-winning keeper can retire at the end of the season, Ulreich calling it a day on his career is also a possibility. “I can’t speak for Manu about what happens after the season, but it’s not like I’m making everything dependent on him,” he added.

Recent findings suggest that sitting on an expiring contract, the 38-year-old is open to anything that might happen going forward and understands things can change rapidly. “Anything is possible as long as I feel good, healthy, and fit. That’s the case at the moment. But I’ve also learned that things can change quickly. I live in the here and now, and right now I enjoy going out on the pitch every day,” he explained.

It has been revealed that bayern may struggle to find a reliable keeper like Ulreich, who admits that giving it your best in training and keeping the No.1 on their toes comes as part of the parcel. “It’s vital to always try to deliver strong performances in training,” he said. “If only to show the goalkeeper in front of you, ‘hey, you have to give your all.’.

“He should also signal to the team that there’s someone back there who gives top performances in every training session.”.

While 23-year-old keeper Urbig is expected to be the long-term replacement for Neuer, Bayern are still looking for a good backup keeper – Finn Dahmen of Augsburg, Marvin Schwäbe of Cologne, and Loris Karius of Schalke, according to Bild’s ‘Bayern Insider’ podcast.

  • Perhaps even more significant than the result was the manner in which Bremen dominated their northern rivals.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, werder Bremen secured a memorable 4-0 victory over Hamburg in the 111th Bundesliga edition of the Nordderby. Marco Friedl, Justin Njinmah and Niclas Füllkrug all scored during an outstanding second-half performance at the Weserstadion, as Daniel Thioune’s side returned to winning ways following their defeat against Stuttgart.

Perhaps even more significant than the result was the manner in which Bremen dominated their northern rivals.

After a goalless first half, Bremen broke the deadlock through captain Friedl in the 55th minute before Njinmah scored twice in four minutes to put the result beyond doubt. For Njinmah, who was making his first start since suffering an injury towards the end of August, his brace represented a particularly encouraging return.

Füllkrug completed the scoring in stoppage time, taking his Bundesliga tally to 10 goals in 10 matches since returning to Bremen.

Industry observers note that werder finished with 56% possession and seven shots on target compared to Hamburg’s one. Their attacking efficiency and defensive organisation made the difference.

The victory came just one day after Bremen announced that Thioune had agreed to extend his contract. There could hardly have been a better way to celebrate that announcement.

Bremen remain unbeaten at the Weserstadion this season, collecting 13 points from a possible 15 and winning nine of their last 10 Bundesliga home encounters against Hamburg.

For Merlin Polzin, the defeat highlighted Hamburg’s persistent problems away from home, having now lost five of their six away league matches this season.

Bremen, meanwhile, continue to demonstrate how much progress they have made under Thioune. Their ability to remain patient, maintain defensive discipline and exploit opportunities in the second half reflects a team growing in confidence.

With 18 points from 10 matches, Werder have given their supporters genuine reasons for optimism. European qualification may still be a premature expectation, but performances like this suggest Bremen are gradually becoming a team capable of competing for considerably more than Bundesliga survival.

For now, however, northern Germany belongs to Werder Bremen.

Recent findings suggest that E' un pareggio, ma sa di sconfitta. Perché? Molto semplice: passando da Bergamo puoi anche tollerare un inciampo, ma il vero problema riguarda come questo risultato è maturato. Sarà oggetto di riflessione già da oggi ad Appiano Gentile, con il solito asterisco: il tempo per sistemare le cose, se non direttamente in campo, è ridotto al midollo. Mercoledì al Meazza arriverà lo Stoccarda in Champions League, prima del doppio impegno in tre giorni, tra sabato e martedì prossimo, contro il Genoa tra campionato e Coppa Italia. Gli allenamenti non saranno tantissimi, ma Chivu dovrà farseli bastare.

Anche perché certi problemi, tornati a galla ieri sera contro l'Atalanta, sono già noti a tutti in casa nerazzurra. L'atteggiamento molto spesso non riesce a essere quello giusto dal primo all'ultimo minuto. Dopo aver sofferto a lungo di mancanza di adeguata concentrazione all'inizio delle partite, la squadra nerazzurra ieri alla Fresh Balance Arena si è ingiustificatamente sentita appagata prima del tempo e per più volte nell'arco della stessa gara. Il primo campanello d'allarme è suonato sullo 0-2, quando con troppa facilità la squadra ha concesso all'Atalanta di tornare in partita con il gol evitabile segnato da Elmas. La stessa cosa è successa anche nella ripresa, quando - non si capisce il perché - i Campioni d'Italia hanno evidentemente pensato di aver già vinto una sfida che ha presentato poi il conto quasi sul gong.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Chelsea are promising to be this season’s Premier League entertainers and yet manager Xabi Alonso seemingly believes less is more when it comes to possession.
  • Industry observers note that alonso has started with two wins from two league games in charge of Chelsea, with his team scoring seven goals and conceding five.
  • Recent findings suggest that but perhaps the most significant numbers are around how much – or how little – Chelsea are having the ball.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chelsea are promising to be this season’s Premier League entertainers and yet manager Xabi Alonso seemingly believes less is more when it comes to possession.

Industry observers note that alonso has started with two wins from two league games in charge of Chelsea, with his team scoring seven goals and conceding five. So far, it has been a lot of fun – if not entirely convincing.

Recent findings suggest that but perhaps the most significant numbers are around how much – or how little – Chelsea are having the ball. Having finished their 3-2 victory over Fulham with 38.11 per cent of possession, Chelsea had just 25.6 per cent in the 4-3 success over Brighton and Hove Albion and successfully completed 146 passes. Both were their lowest figures on record in the Premier League.

“The data is not important,” Alonso said. “It’s how you play and what we can do better. I don’t say ‘today we need to have 60 per cent or 20 per cent’. I never talk about those things. It’s about how to prepare, how to be more competitive.”.

Industry observers note that chelsea’s third goal against Brighton, scored in the 32nd minute, best summed up the London club under Alonso to date. It took the home side three passes to go from the edge of their own penalty area to João Pedro scoring against his former club.

Jorrel Hato passed the ball to Morgan Rogers, he then released Hato down the left and the wing-back slid the ball across for João Pedro to finish. It was a devastating counter-attack and should have put Chelsea on course for a much easier win.

Joao Pedro finishes off a deadly Chelsea counter-attack and gives the Blues a 3-0 lead 🔥 pic.twitter.com/wAr0ckIgXJ.

“After 30 minutes, we are 3-0 and probably, in that moment, we have played too much the result,” Alonso remarked. “It’s quite normal, it happens in many teams. I am sure in the future we can manage it better.”.

It is one thing outscoring Fulham and a depleted Brighton team without having the ball, but can Chelsea do that against the bigger and better teams? We will get an early indicator in the next game against Arsenal at the Emirates.

Alonso’s approach has some similarities to the way in which Antonio Conte set up his Chelsea title-winning team. Just as Conte converted Victor Moses into an effective right wing-back, Alonso started Pedro Neto there on Sunday.

After Roméo Lavia had opened the scoring, it was Neto who grabbed Chelsea’s second goal against Brighton by drifting into the penalty area to finish from Rogers’s low cross.

"It's a nightmare for the goalkeeper!"Bart Verbruggen and Mats Wieffer's collision leads to Romeo Lavia scoring his first goal for Chelsea ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/q5awbdwVV0.

Industry observers note that "Pedro Neto Pounces!"Morgan Rogers goes past his defender before sliding the ball across to Neto! 💥 pic.twitter.com/WHZCIGsOLl.

But whereas Conte’s team gave up little at the back, Alonso’s Chelsea are yet to balance their effective transitional play with shutting out their opponents.

Neto was partly to blame for Brighton’s first goal, as he missed a challenge in the build-up to Malick Yalcouyé’s brilliant volley. Making his Chelsea debut, goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez could do nothing to stop it and can expect to be kept busy this season if things do not change.

“I have come here to challenge and to try and win the Premier League,” Martínez said. “I know the talent we have up front. I try to bring that solidity at the back.”.

"Yalcouye with a sumptuous volley!"Malick Yalcouye puts Brighton on the scoreboard with a venomous volley 😳 pic.twitter.com/8UeeyvPjUw.

Industry observers note that conte’s Chelsea had N’Golo Kanté to mop up in midfield and that is an area of the pitch that is causing Alonso some difficulties. Manchester City target Enzo Fernández was once again left out of the squad and Moisés Caicedo was not deemed fit enough to start.

It has been revealed that caicedo was eventually thrown on when Chelsea were trying to stop Brighton completing a remarkable comeback, but he was swiftly forced off again with an injury. The club have been exploring a move for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara and that need looks even more pressing now.

Recent findings suggest that “We want the best for the team and that’s why we took a decision [on Fernández] against Luton and today,” Alonso remarked. “What’s going to develop? We’re not sure. We can prepare. We are preparing for all the scenarios. But I assure you that whatever happens, from Wednesday [when the transfer window is shut] we’ll have a good enough squad to compete in all the Premier League games.”.

Chelsea’s fresh set-piece coach Austin MacPhee had celebrated Lavia’s goal, which came partly as a result of a corner but owed more to a mistake from Brighton goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen.

MacPhee, however, will not have liked Brighton’s second-half goals. It was from a short corner that the visitors managed to work the ball to Pascal Gross and his cross was diverted into his own net by João Pedro.

Joao Pedro puts Pascal Groß's cross into his own net and Brighton have brought it back to 3-2 👀 pic.twitter.com/maBMwVu3DC.

Gross’s headed third goal also came at the end of a set-piece, but, fortunately for Chelsea, it was in the sixth minute of added time and Cole Palmer had already made the points safe for the home team before then.

Palmer had done little to impress watching England head coach Thomas Tuchel until he picked up the ball in the 74th minute, shrugged off two Brighton challenges and produced a brilliant finish to beat Verbruggen.

Cole Palmer finishes EXPERTLY to give Chelsea their two-goal cushion back 💥 pic.twitter.com/6xI9W8xe2q.

Fabian Hürzeler, the Brighton manager, mentioned his team “dominated” the game, but acknowledged: “I think if you spend so much money on these kinds of players, like Rogers, Palmer or João [Pedro], then, of course, a team like Chelsea can rely on this individual quality. And they indicated it in certain moments of the game.”.

According to recent reports, palmer, João Pedro and Rogers are clearly going to be a huge problem for Chelsea’s opponents. But Alonso’s team cannot rely on having to score three or four goals to win games. And they might need to have a bit more of the ball.

"The game today was a special game for me." João Pedro claims he was happy with his performance for Chelsea against Brighton 🔵 pic.twitter.com/fWSqWo7ert.

Recent findings suggest that 6 - João Pedro today was the sixth player (and first for Chelsea) to score a goal, assist a goal, and score an own goal in the same Premier League game, and first since Tottenham Hotspur's Son Heung-min against Man City in December 2023.Eventful. pic.twitter.com/xRVjqkOY9D.

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta stated that Ethan Nwaneri, who is currently on loan at Borussia Dortmund from the Gunners, needs to earn the right to play.

Industry observers note that “He had started playing quite a lot, and now recently he hasn’t played that much,” the Spaniard said at Monday’s press conference ahead of their UEFA Champions League clash on Tuesday. “He needs to earn the right to play because he is playing at the top of the Bundesliga and the players that they have, they have huge talent and quality. That is the reality of football: you go there, and because you come from Arsenal, it doesn’t give you any advantage so you need to earn it.”.

Nwaneri has only played six minutes of football in Dortmund’s last three games, and has only registered one assist – which came on his Bundesliga debut against Hoffenheim – since his arrival from Arsenal.

Sources indicate that arteta, though, believes the 19-year-old is capable of turning around his current situation. “Ethan first of all has the mindset to do it and then the quality to do it. These things are part of a journey and part of a season, and earn the right to win.”.

Recent findings suggest that nwaneri could potentially face Arsenal on Tuesday at the Emirates as there is no restriction in his loan deal that prevents him from playing against his parent club. Whether Niko Kovač opts to use him in the game remains to be seen.

Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya will be unavailable for Tuesday’s UEFA Champions League game against Borussia Dortmund after suffering an injury in his side’s 2-2 draw against Newcastle United on Saturday.

It has been revealed that speaking on the injury, Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta mentioned: “He is not fit for tomorrow, unfortunately, but it doesn’t look too serious. It has been revealed that fellow Spanish keeper Kepa Arrizabalaga, who came on in the Newcastle game, is expected to start tomorrow. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta had positive words to say about Borussia Dortmund ahead of Tuesday’s UEFA Champions League game clash.

“I am very impressed with them, and you see their results so far, where they are in the Bundesliga and where they are in the Champions League – the way they are playing, the way they are dominating games,” the Spaniard told reporters at Monday’s press conference.

It has been revealed that arteta also recalled the pre-season game the two teams had. “We had them here in pre-season, and they revealed their quality and what they are capable of, so we are very much aware of that, but we will play at home in front of our crowd and go and attack the game; that’s for sure,” he added.

In a recent development, the two sides met in pre-season in the Emirates Cup where Dortmund came out 3-2 winners. Before that, the last time the two teams faced each other was back in 2014 in the Champions League group stage when BVB beat Arsenal 2-0 at home before losing away by the same scoreline.

Unbeaten in this season’s competition, Arsenal sit third in the league phase standings on 10 points, while Dortmund sit 12th on nine points.

Nel recupero l’islandese trova lo spazio alle spalle della difesa, evita Falcone e deposita il pallone in rete. La partenza in posizione di fuorigioco rende però vano il suo tentativo. FEATURE | 5 standout players from Bundesliga, Matchday 10

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (648 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Getfootballnewsgermany

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bundesliga Matchday 10 delivered an eventful return from the international break, with Werder Bremen dominating the Nordderby, RB Leipzig scoring five against Union Berlin and Bayer Leverkusen recording an emphatic victory over Paderborn.
  • Elsewhere, Borussia Dortmund went top after overcoming Borussia Mönchengladbach as Bayern Munich dropped points against Cologne, while Augsburg ended their seven-match winless run against Mainz.
  • Here are five players whose individual performances made the difference for their teams….
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bundesliga Matchday 10 delivered an eventful return from the international break, with Werder Bremen dominating the Nordderby, RB Leipzig scoring five against Union Berlin and Bayer Leverkusen recording an emphatic victory over Paderborn.

Elsewhere, Borussia Dortmund went top after overcoming Borussia Mönchengladbach as Bayern Munich dropped points against Cologne, while Augsburg ended their seven-match winless run against Mainz.

Here are five players whose individual performances made the difference for their teams….

Justin Njinmah produced one of the outstanding performances of Matchday 10 as Werder Bremen dismantled Hamburg 4-0 at the Weserstadion.

Making his first start since suffering an injury in August, Njinmah scored twice in four minutes during the second half. His goals in the 66th and 70th minutes ended any realistic possibility of a Hamburg comeback after Marco Friedl had opened the scoring.

While Niclas Füllkrug completed the victory with his 10th Bundesliga goal of the season, Njinmah was the standout performer.

His pace, directness and finishing provide Daniel Thioune with another dangerous attacking option alongside Füllkrug. His return to fitness could prove particularly key as Bremen look to maintain their impressive start to the campaign.

Afonso Moreira delivered an impressive performance as Bayer Leverkusen defeated newly promoted Paderborn 4-0 at the BayArena.

The Portuguese winger opened the scoring in the 14th minute before doubling Leverkusen’s advantage shortly after half-time. Patrik Schick and Ezequiel Fernández subsequently completed the scoring.

Moreira’s brace demonstrated his attacking potential and ability to make decisive contributions in the final third.

For Leverkusen, having additional goalscoring threats alongside Schick could prove essential in their pursuit of Champions League qualification. Moreira’s performance was an encouraging indication that he can provide precisely that.

Brajan Gruda continued his impressive development as RB Leipzig secured a commanding 5-1 victory over Union Berlin.

With Leipzig leading 2-1, Gruda scored in the 72nd minute to give Martín Demichelis’ side some breathing room. Rocco Reitz and Ridle Baku subsequently added further goals to complete an outstanding second-half performance.

Following his impressive display against Augsburg before the international break, Gruda is becoming an increasingly influential figure in Leipzig’s attack.

In a recent development, his technical ability, creativity and willingness to take on defenders give Leipzig an notable attacking alternative. Demichelis’ praise following the match further underlined the growing importance of the young German international.

Michael Gregoritsch was instrumental in Augsburg’s much-needed 3-1 victory over Mainz, ending a seven-match Bundesliga winless run.

In a recent development, the Austrian international opened the scoring in the 19th minute before completing his brace shortly after half-time. Juma Bah also scored for Augsburg, while Mainz reduced the deficit through Ransford-Yeboah Königsdörffer.

Gregoritsch’s two goals took his Bundesliga tally to seven this season, highlighting his importance to Augsburg despite their difficult start to the campaign.

For a team struggling to establish consistency, having an experienced centre-forward capable of delivering in decisive moments could prove fundamental to their survival ambitions.

Jonathan Burkardt once again demonstrated his importance to Eintracht Frankfurt by scoring the only goal in their 1-0 victory over Hoffenheim.

The German international broke the deadlock in the 25th minute, securing three valuable points for Adi Hütter’s side in a difficult encounter at Deutsche Bank Park.

Following his brace against Paderborn before the international break, Burkardt has now scored three goals across his last two Bundesliga appearances.

Frankfurt’s inconsistent start has raised questions about their European ambitions, but Burkardt’s goalscoring form remains one of the most encouraging aspects of Hütter’s rebuilding project. His ability to decide tight matches could prove essential as Frankfurt look to climb the Bundesliga table.

Matchday 10 highlighted the importance of players delivering in different circumstances. Njinmah enjoyed a memorable comeback in the Nordderby, Moreira showcased his attacking potential, Gruda continued his development, Gregoritsch helped Augsburg end their winless run and Burkardt secured an key victory for Frankfurt. All five produced performances worthy of recognition following the international break.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scegli Fcinter1908.it come tuo sito preferito su Google: clicca qui.

Intervenuti su Youtube, Gianpaolo Calvarese e Piero Giacomelli hanno commentato il rigore dato all'Inter contro l'Atalanta.

Calvarese: "Tanti episodi per Maresca che ha fatto bene, alcuni episodi davvero complessi dal punto di vista regolamentare".

Giacomelli: "Mi è piaciuto l'atteggiamento, in certe cose mi rivedo, la calma, la tranquillità. Mi piace da morire chi riesce ad essere calmo in campo, nelle fasi finali del match lo è stato".

Calvarese: "Grande personalità, anche se ogni tanto esagera ma devo dire che si è messo un po' in linea, quando sta bene è imbattibile. Il primo calcio di rigore è strano, Zappacosta si appoggia a terra con un movimento naturale, secondo me il primo braccio non è punibile ma c'è un extra movimento, non voglio sapere se istintivo o volontario, ma quel movimento è punibile".

Recent findings suggest that giacomelli: "Su questo ci sono pochi dubbi, il movimento è innaturale e punibile, si accorge di aver fatto una frittata, Zappacosta avrebbe preferito prendere un rosso perché per un difensore prendere giallo significa che quella palla non sarebbe entrata in porta, cosa che invece le immagini testimoniano. Dal punto di vista calcistico, il calciatore è contento di aver preso il giallo ma pensa che l'arbitro l'abbia reputata, secondo me in maniera corretta, una palla che non stava entrando".

Calvarese: "C'è una certezza: quel movimento fa sì che il VAR avalli la decisione. Non so se Maresca abbia fischiato il primo o il secondo movimento, mi rimane il dubbio. Ma sono convinto che il secondo movimento abbia levato ogni dubbio al VAR che quindi non è intervenuto".

Giacomelli: "Maresca è messo talmente bene che vede bene, noi vediamo la main, lui ha una reverse, il secondo movimento lo vede meglio di sicuro e per lui è molto più semplice di quanto non lo sia in TV".

Calvarese: "Non è cartellino rosso in ogni caso, fughiamo ogni dubbio perché ho sentito tanti che chiedevano il rosso".

Manchester United’s attack may be their best form of defence this season

💡 Key Takeaways
